title: TweenService
summary: Animates properties smoothly over time: TweenService:Create(instance, TweenInfo, goal) builds a Tween you Play — moving parts, fading GUIs, growing HealthBars, without per-frame math.

methods.name: Create
methods.signature: TweenService:Create(instance: Instance, tweenInfo: TweenInfo, goal: { [string]: any }) --> Tween
methods.description: Builds a Tween that will animate the listed properties from current values to the goal values. Does NOT start it — call Tween:Play().

methods.name: GetValue
methods.signature: TweenService:GetValue(alpha: number, easingStyle: Enum.EasingStyle, easingDirection: Enum.EasingDirection) --> number
methods.description: Easing math helper: normalized progress in → eased value out.

details.heading: TweenInfo
details.body: `TweenInfo.new(time, easingStyle, easingDirection, repeatCount, reverses, delayTime)` — duration in seconds, curve (Linear, Quad, Bounce, Elastic…), direction (In/Out/InOut), repeats (-1 = infinite), reverse flag, start delay.

details.heading: Tween object
details.body: Returned by Create: `Play()`, `Pause()`, `Cancel()`, `PlaybackState`, and the `Completed` event (fires with Enum.PlaybackState when finished/cancelled). Tweens on the client animate client-side.

details.heading: Tweenable properties
details.body: Most numeric/visual datatypes: number, bool→no; Color3, UDim2, Vector3, CFrame (no rotation interpolation — use Orientation/align instead), NumberSequence, ColorSequence, Rect, etc. Property names in the goal table must be actual properties of the instance.

explanation.whatItIs: The 'slide it over there smoothly' service. You say where a property should end up and how long to take; TweenService interpolates every frame in between.
explanation.whyItExists: Hand-writing RunService lerp loops for every animation is tedious and error-prone. Tweens package it: duration + curve + goal.
whenToUse: Fading GUI elements (menus in/out), sliding frames
whenNotToUse: Physics-driven motion — tweens override physics; don't tween things that should collide naturally
Tight per-frame control needs (procedural aiming) — RunService loops fit better
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
TweenService:Create(part, TweenInfo.new(1, Bounce, Out),
                    { Position = targetPos })
        │
        ▼
    Tween ──Play()──▶ frames interpolate automatically
        │
        ▼  (1 second later)
    Completed fires → part is exactly at targetPos
```
tips: Reuse one Tween by calling Play() again (it replays from current values only after Cancel/reset — recreate when goals change)
`tween.Completed:Wait()` yields until done — chains beautifully inside task.spawn
GUI fades: tween BackgroundTransparency and TextTransparency together
EasingStyle.Sine/Quad InOut feels natural for UI; Bounce/Elastic for juice
commonMistakes: Tweening a property the instance doesn't have → error
Expecting server tweens to be smooth on all clients for physics objects (networked part ownership can conflict)
Tweens on properties that also change elsewhere fighting each other

examples.title: Sliding a GUI frame in
examples.code:
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local frame = script.Parent   -- a Frame off-screen to the left

local info = TweenInfo.new(
    0.4,                              -- seconds
    Enum.EasingStyle.Quad,
    Enum.EasingDirection.Out
)

local goal = { Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5) }  -- centered
local tween = TweenService:Create(frame, info, goal)
tween:Play()

tween.Completed:Connect(function()
    print("Menu finished sliding in")
end)
examples.whyItWorks: The goal table names real properties of a Frame; TweenService drives Position from its current value to center over 0.4s with an ease-out curve.

examples.title: A bouncing coin pickup effect
examples.code:
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local function coinPop(coin: Part)
    local pop = TweenService:Create(coin, TweenInfo.new(0.3, Enum.EasingStyle.Back, Enum.EasingDirection.Out),
        { Size = coin.Size * 1.4 })
    local shrink = TweenService:Create(coin, TweenInfo.new(0.2),
        { Size = Vector3.new(0.1, 0.1, 0.1), Transparency = 1 })

    pop:Play()
    pop.Completed:Connect(function()
        shrink:Play()
    end)
    shrink.Completed:Connect(function()
        coin:Destroy()
    end)
end
